Employer training prospects

Broad local PostgreSQL evidence for pharmaceutical analytics training, early-career pathways and employer outreach.

This analysis broadens the original selected-employer inventory using the local PostgreSQL collection. It identifies advertisements and employer labels that warrant review for pharmaceutical analytics training. It separates student pathways, early-career hiring signals and experienced roles so that company-sponsored employee development can be assessed alongside graduate recruitment.

A prospect is not a committed buyer. Job advertisements reveal tasks and qualification signals; they do not measure the number of current employees eligible for training, the employer’s budget or its willingness to sponsor a cohort.

Snapshot extracted 2026-11-06 UTC from local PostgreSQL. All available dates were scanned, including missing posting dates.

These counts cover matching records across employers, not a census of pharmaceutical companies. A posting can mention a pharmaceutical client while its employer belongs to another industry. Employer-text and industry-code signals are screening evidence, not independent industry verification.

Of the US analytics matches, 2,203 have source posting dates within 120 days of extraction; 1,509 have no posting date and remain included. 0 have dates later than extraction and are excluded from the recent-date measure. Dates do not verify that a role is still open.

The 0–3-year bucket identifies advertisements for review; it does not establish eligibility. Degree alternatives, specialist requirements and postgraduate study can change suitability. Internships are separate from employee-upskilling prospects. Missing experience evidence stays unknown. Age requirements such as “18 years or older” are excluded.

Enrichment status describes pipeline processing, not independently verified correctness.

Combined 357,230 source rows into 288,681 posting identities using source IDs, normalized requisition URLs and same-employer database duplicate links. This prospect screen requires an analytical title; duty-only matches, pharmacy data-entry and non-analytical support titles are withheld for manual review; explicit foreign recruiting-country codes override contradictory US evidence. Named employer references use the existing reviewed inventory and MassBio shortlist. Employer names are whitespace/case normalized only; subsidiaries, spelling variants and unnamed employers may remain separate. A shared title alone does not join advertisements. Conflicting US/non-US evidence is withheld from the US subset.

Industry-code enrichments are unvalidated and do not establish company membership. Original descriptions drive analytics and skill screening; enriched qualification summaries are used only when original text is absent. This is a reproducible rules-based screen; individual matches require review before outreach or eligibility decisions.

Use the evidence for company training

  1. Review the source advertisements behind a company’s early-career commercial-data count. Confirm that the work fits the proposed curriculum, including data integration, SQL, business intelligence, source quality and communication.
  2. Separate graduate recruiting and student internships from existing employee development. Verify degree alternatives, actual work experience and required domain expertise in the complete source text.
  3. Ask the analytics manager and learning-and-development sponsor about the team, recurring skill gaps, suitable employees, release time and budget. Record those answers separately from posting counts.
  4. Prioritize a pilot only after the employer identifies staff and a sponsor. Measure assessed work and employer feedback; this dataset cannot establish training uptake or certificate outcomes.

The existing job explorer remains the original selected-employer comparison. These broader local-only results are a separate saved extraction and should not be added to that inventory without reconciling overlap.
